references.text: The law regarding the bride-price (mohar) for a virgin who has been seduced. The man must pay fifty shekels of silver to her father and take her as his wife.
A parallel law concerning a man who lies with a virgin and must pay the bride-price and marry her.
Shechem offers to pay the bride-price (mohar) and gifts for Dinah, illustrating the cultural practice of bride-price.
Jacob offers seven years of service as a bride-price for Rachel, which illustrates the bride-price system.
Saul demands one hundred Philistine foreskins as a bride-price for Michal, showing that the bride-price could take forms other than money.
The previous verse describes how a man who seduces a virgin must marry her, while this verse provides an exception if her father refuses.
